paper_id: Data-Locality-Aware Task Assignment and Scheduling for Distributed Job Executions
title: Data-Locality-Aware Task Assignment and Scheduling for Distributed Job Executions
motivation: Cloud jobs require data chunks replicated across servers; inefficient data-locality scheduling increases transfer overhead and violates SLAs.
problem_framing: Bipartite graph-based task assignment minimizing job completion time under FIFO or prioritized reordering, without future job knowledge.
key_insight: Water-filling achieves tight K-approximation where K is task group count; replica-deletion leverages global optimization to surpass WF.
method_signature: OBTA narrows search via bounds; WF water-fills across groups; RD deletes replicas globally; OCWF-ACC adds early-exit.
evaluation_criteria: Average job completion time, computation overhead, CDF of completion times on Alibaba cluster trace.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Theoretical performance analysis of RD is left as future work.
evidence_for_taste: without prior knowledge of future job arrivals
thinking_moves: Identify limitations of prior work (SWAG neglects replication, offline methods lack adaptability)
Prove tight approximation bounds on algorithm behavior
Narrow solution search space via upper/lower bounds on completion time
Extend homogeneous algorithm to heterogeneous setting with formal proof
Design heuristic using global view rather than local sequential processing
